faq.q: Can I make before-and-after videos for a skincare product?
faq.a: We’d steer away from it for skin results. A generated face is not evidence of what your product does, and a visible change in skin can read as a promise. Show application, texture, and packaging instead, and leave claims about results out of your request and the claims you use in an ad.

faq.q: Will the video match my exact foundation or lipstick shade?
faq.a: Color comes from your photo and your wording, so shoot in daylight and name the shade plainly, like "warm beige liquid" or "brick red matte." If the tone still drifts, generate another version; the credit cost is shown before each one.

faq.q: Can I add my price or a promo code to the image?
faq.a: Type prices, promo codes, and product names on afterward in Canva or CapCut. Lettering made by AI can come out misspelled, so keep the image clean and add the words yourself.

faq.q: What kind of product photo should I upload for skincare?
faq.a: A straight-on shot with the label toward the camera, on a plain surface, with no hands or clutter in the frame. Glossy tubes and clear glass pick up glare, so shoot beside a window rather than using flash.

faq.q: How long should a beauty ad video be?
faq.a: Pick 6, 10, or 15 seconds for feed ads that lead with one action, such as a swatch or a pump. Use 30 seconds when you want a longer routine; the credit cost is shown before each length.

faq.q: Can I use the same product photo for a white background shot and a routine video?
faq.a: Yes. Shoot the bottle, tube or jar straight-on with the whole label visible, and use that file for both the white background photo and any routine or demo video. Keep the original uncropped so the vertical video can reframe without cutting the cap.

faq.q: Do beauty ads need a person in the frame?
faq.a: Ad scenes such as GRWM, reviews and shade checks read better with an adult person or hand using the product. Use object-only white background shots for the listing, and reserve shelf or vanity stills for moments where the package itself is the subject.

faq.q: Can I run the videos as paid beauty ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloaded clips are watermark-free and licensed for commercial use, including paid social ads. Before-and-after skin results should be avoided, since they can read as a result claim; any text you add must be accurate and pass ad review.

faq.q: Is an AI creator video different from hiring a real UGC creator?
faq.a: Yes. You upload one photo and pay credits per clip instead of paying a creator's rate, usage fees, and revision rounds. The person is AI-generated and not a real customer, so present the video as an ad rather than an independent review.
